Marten CVE-2026-45288 regConfig SQL injection attempt in web traffic AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP requests carrying the high-fidelity Marten full-text-search regConfig SQL injection signature. The PostgreSQL `::regconfig` type-cast literal, `to_tsvector('` fragment, and DDL/DML targeting Marten's `mt_doc_*` document tables are essentially never present in benign user input, making this near-zero-FP exploitation telemetry. Rationale: The `::regconfig` PostgreSQL type-cast literal is the exact fragment Marten's `FullTextWhereFragment.cs` interpolates around the user-supplied regConfig value (per the patched source and PR #4343). It cannot appear in legitimate URL query strings because no client UI emits a PostgreSQL type cast. Paired with `to_tsvector('`, `pg_sleep(`, and the Marten-specific `mt_doc_` table prefix, this is near-zero-FP exploitation telemetry. Corroborated against the canonical advisory and Marten source. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vmw2-qwm8-x84c • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/pull/4343 • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/blob/master/src/Marten/Linq/SqlGeneration/Filters/FullTextWhereFragment.cs
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized internal penetration test or DAST scan (Burp, sqlmap) running CVE-2026-45288 payloads against your own app
  • Security research / threat-intel team replaying the public PoC in a staging environment
  • WAF / vendor security scanner emitting the payload as part of its baseline test suite
  • Developer pasting the GHSA advisory text into a search field that is logged verbatim (low likelihood)
Suppression filter
| where ClientIP !in (dynamic(["<allowlisted-pentest-IP-1>", "<dast-scanner-IP-2>"]))
| where UA !has_any ("sqlmap", "Burp", "nuclei", "acunetix", "qualys")  // optionally — remove to keep these in scope when they're external
Response runbook
1. Triage: pivot on ClientIP to check WAF block status and historical reputation; pull the full request body and response status — a 500 with PostgreSQL error noise or a 200 with anomalous response time (>5s for `pg_sleep(5)`) indicates the injection reached the DB. Map the target Host/Url back to a known Marten-backed application and its Marten version. 2. Contain: block the source IP at WAF/CDN, terminate any active app sessions from that source, and if the affected app is still on Marten <= 8.36, deploy the workaround (regConfig allowlist or hard-code) at the application boundary until patch. 3. Hunt: query DB audit logs for `to_tsvector('` calls in the request window (see UC3), check `pg_stat_statements` for unexpected `pg_sleep` / `SELECT version` / DDL against `mt_doc_*` tables, and look for follow-on credential-access or data-exfil queries from the same app-pool DB role.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SqliMarkers = dynamic(["::regconfig", "%3A%3Aregconfig", "%3a%3aregconfig", "pg_sleep(", "DROP TABLE mt_doc_", "drop table mt_doc_", "to_tsvector('", "'; SELECT version", "'::text);"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where csUriQuery has_any (SqliMarkers) or csUriStem has_any (SqliMarkers)
    | extend SourceTable = "W3CIISLog",
             ClientIP = cIP,
             Url = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery),
             UA = csUserAgent,
             Host = sSiteName,
             Status = tostring(scStatus)),
  (AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where CsUriQuery has_any (SqliMarkers) or CsUriStem has_any (SqliMarkers)
    | extend SourceTable = "AppServiceHTTPLogs",
             ClientIP = CIp,
             Url = strcat(CsUriStem, "?", CsUriQuery),
             UA = UserAgent,
             Host = CsHost,
             Status = tostring(ScStatus)),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RequestURL has_any (SqliMarkers) or RequestContext has_any (SqliMarkers)
    | extend SourceTable = strcat(DeviceVendor, "/", DeviceProduct),
             ClientIP = SourceIP,
             Url = RequestURL,
             UA = RequestClientApplication,
             Host = DestinationHostName,
             Status = tostring(EventOutcome))
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, Host, ClientIP, Url, UA, Status
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable Marten library (CVE-2026-45288) present on host — proactive exposure hunt AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunting query that identifies hosts running a vulnerable Marten NuGet library (<= 8.36) so the SOC can scope CVE-2026-45288 exposure and drive patching to 8.36.1+. Combines Defender TVM vulnerability data with on-disk Marten.dll discovery for hosts that TVM doesn't enumerate (build agents, dev workstations, self-hosted .NET app servers). Rationale: Marten is distributed as `Marten.dll` (the canonical NuGet artifact name) and is the only library exposing the vulnerable `FullTextWhereFragment` SQL builder. Microsoft's TVM does not consistently inventory NuGet packages, so the FileEvent/FileWritten fallback catches build agents and self-hosted .NET app servers that wouldn't show up in `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities`. SOC pivot: once a host hits, manually confirm version via the application's `*.deps.json` / `packages.lock.json` (the file lookup doesn't include version metadata). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vmw2-qwm8-x84c • https://www.nuget.org/packages/Marten
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer workstations with Marten source clones or sample apps (legitimate but should be tracked)
  • CI build agents that pull Marten as a transitive dependency for short-lived test jobs
  • Hosts running Marten 8.36.1+ (patched) where Marten.dll exists but is NOT vulnerable — must check version
  • Decommissioned app servers with stale Marten.dll files no longer in production use

1. Triage: for each hit, identify the parent .NET application (look at the FolderPath — typically `<app>\bin\<framework>\Marten.dll`) and confirm Marten version by reading the adjacent `<app>.deps.json` or `packages.lock.json`. Vulnerable: Marten <= 8.36. 2. Contain: for any app surfacing the `regConfig` parameter to untrusted input (review controller / minimal-API endpoints for `?lang=`, `?regConfig=`, or model-bound full-text-search calls), deploy the workaround at the application boundary (regex allowlist `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(\.[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)?$`) until upgrade. 3. Hunt: schedule patch to 8.36.1+; pivot UC1 web-log queries against the application's hostname for the prior 30 days to check for exploitation that pre-dates this discovery.

Marten CVE-2026-45288 injection observed executing in PostgreSQL audit log AIExploitation High
Detects PostgreSQL server-side log entries that contain the Marten full-text-search SQL signature (`to_tsvector('`) interleaved with attacker-injected payloads (`pg_sleep(`, DDL against `mt_doc_*`, appended SELECT statements). This catches successful exploitation that reached the DB, including via app paths that don't traverse the perimeter WAF. Rationale: Per the GHSA advisory and patched `FullTextWhereFragment.cs`, every Marten full-text-search call emits SQL of shape `to_tsvector('<regConfig>'::regconfig, <data>) @@ ...('<regConfig>'::regconfig, ?)`. The verbatim `to_tsvector('` plus the article's PoC payload fragments (`pg_sleep`, `DROP TABLE mt_doc_`, `'::text);`) in the same log line means the injection successfully reached PostgreSQL's parser. The `mt_doc_` document-table prefix is specific to Marten's storage convention (corroborated via Marten's own full-text-index integration tests). Defender XDR and Falcon FDR do not ingest PostgreSQL server logs so those fields are empty. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vmw2-qwm8-x84c • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/pull/4343 • https://github.com/JasperFx/marten/blob/master/src/DocumentDbTests/Indexes/full_text_index.cs
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized DBA pasting / replaying CVE-2026-45288 PoC payloads inside the DB for vulnerability validation
  • Regression tests (Marten's own `full_text_regconfig_sql_injection.cs` suite) executing against a non-prod replica that ships logs to the same SIEM
  • DBA `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` runs against attacker queries captured from earlier audit logs
  • Backup-restore operations replaying historical query traffic in a recovery environment
Suppression filter
| where Detail !contains "application_name=psql"  // optional: exclude DBA interactive shell sessions when they're authorized — confirm the DBA list before applying
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the full log line plus surrounding 30s window — extract the database user, client_addr, application_name, and full statement text; correlate `application_name` back to the offending app pool / service account. Pivot UC1 against the same time window to find the originating HTTP request and client IP. 2. Contain: terminate the active DB session (`pg_terminate_backend(pid)`), rotate the application's DB role credentials, and either revoke unnecessary privileges (DROP, CREATE) from the app role or block the WAF / app boundary as per UC2 workaround. 3. Hunt: review `pg_stat_statements` / pgaudit for the past 30 days for additional `to_tsvector('` queries with anomalous shapes; check for any successful DDL against `mt_doc_*` tables, SELECT statements against `pg_user`/`pg_shadow`/`information_schema`, or `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM` / `lo_export` attempts indicating post-injection RCE pivots.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let DbSqliMarkers = dynamic(["pg_sleep(", "DROP TABLE mt_doc_", "drop table mt_doc_", "'; SELECT version", "'::text); SELECT", "'::text);SELECT", "'::text);"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ProcessName has_any ("postgres", "postgresql", "postmaster")
    | where SyslogMessage has "to_tsvector('"
    | where SyslogMessage has_any (DbSqliMarkers)
    | extend SourceTable = "Syslog",
             Host = Computer,
             Detail = SyslogMessage),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DeviceProduct has_any ("postgres", "postgresql", "pgaudit")
    | where Message has "to_tsvector('"
    | where Message has_any (DbSqliMarkers)
    | extend SourceTable = strcat(DeviceVendor, "/", DeviceProduct),
             Host = DeviceAddress,
             Detail = Message)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, Host, Detail
| order by TimeGenerated desc

MCPHub SSE endpoint accessed with arbitrary username in URL path (CVE-2025/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf hunt) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the vulnerable MCPHub URL pattern `/<user>/sse[/<group>]` on web access logs. Because the username segment is taken straight from the path with no auth, any GET to this pattern from a low-volume / non-allow-listed source — or with an unusual `<user>` token — is the primary spoofing signal pre-patch (< 0.12.15). Rationale: Lifted the literal vulnerable route `/:user/sse/:group(.*)?` from src/server.ts (lines 132-161) and the PoC URL `http://TARGET:3100/CEO-admin-impersonated/sse` directly. Cross-checked at cvereports.com and vulert.com — both confirm the URL shape is the attack surface and that any unauthenticated GET to it creates a session. Defender XDR has no native web-access table for an internal Node.js app, hence empty defender_kql. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-WF8Q-WVV8-P8JF • https://vulert.com/vuln-db/-samanhappy-mcphub--sse-endpoint-accepts-arbitrary-username-from-url-path-without-authentication--en---
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate MCPHub clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, internal AI agents) connecting under valid usernames after upgrade to 0.12.15 with bearer auth disabled
  • Internal load-balancer / Kubernetes ingress health probes that pre-warm the SSE path
  • SAST / DAST scanners (Nuclei, Burp, ZAP) hitting the path as part of authorized scanning windows
  • Application performance monitoring (Datadog Synthetics, Pingdom) configured against /<user>/sse for uptime checks
  • Pre-patch legitimate use — the vulnerable code path was the documented integration route for MCPHub
Suppression filter
// Suppress known internal scanners + health probes + the post-patch known-good user roster
| where SrcIP !in ("10.0.0.50","10.0.0.51") // synthetic-monitoring jump boxes
| where UA !has "DatadogSynthetics" and UA !has "Pingdom" and UA !has "kube-probe"
| extend KnownUser = UserSegment in~ ("alice","bob","svc-mcp-prod")  // populated from IdentityInfo
| where not KnownUser
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull `@samanhappy/mcphub` version from the host (`npm ls @samanhappy/mcphub` or container image label). If < 0.12.15 OR `enableBearerAuth` is false in mcp_settings.json, treat all SSE hits as suspect. Enumerate distinct UserSegment values seen in the last 7 days and compare against the actual IdP user roster. 2. Contain: front MCPHub with auth-required reverse proxy (mTLS or bearer header validation), enforce network ACL so MCPHub only accepts loopback / VPN / known-CIDR clients, upgrade to >= 0.12.15. 3. Hunt: pivot SrcIP → other MCPHub instances in the org, search OfficeActivity / audit logs for tool-call side effects attributed to spoofed users in the same window, and check downstream MCP-server logs (filesystem, GitHub, database connectors) for actions credited to the spoofed identity.
// MCPHub SSE impersonation pattern — pre-patch (< 0.12.15)
// Username taken straight from URL path; any GET to /<user>/sse[/<group>] is the attack shape.
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "GET"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/sse(/.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"^/([^/]+)/sse", 1, csUriStem)
   | extend SourceTable = "W3CIISLog", SrcIP = cIP, Url = strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Method = csMethod, Status = tostring(scStatus), UA = csUserAgent),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/sse(?:/[^?]*)?(?:\?.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/sse", 1, RequestURL)
   | extend SourceTable = "CommonSecurityLog", SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, Method = RequestMethod, Status = tostring(EventOutcome), UA = RequestClientApplication)
| where isnotempty(UserSegment)
| where UserSegment !in~ ("api","static","assets","health","favicon.ico","robots.txt","_next","public")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, SrcIP, Computer, Method, Url, UserSegment, Status, UA

references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf

MCPHub identity spoofing — admin-themed username in /<user>/sse path AIExploitation High
High-fidelity alert for GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf exploitation: requests to MCPHub `/<user>/sse` where the user-segment matches privileged-role keywords (admin, administrator, root, sudo, owner, superuser, sysadmin, ceo, cfo, cto, operator) or the literal PoC string `CEO-admin-impersonated`. Because the segment is taken verbatim as the authenticated identity, an admin-themed token in the path is the cleanest impersonation tell. Rationale: Anchored on the PoC's literal `CEO-admin-impersonated` segment plus the documented impact: 'Impersonate any user, including administrators.' Privileged-role tokens in the URL segment are the highest-signal impersonation indicator because the vulnerable middleware uses the segment verbatim as `IUser.username`. Corroborated against vulert.com and cvereports.com which both echo the admin-impersonation impact. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf • https://vulert.com/vuln-db/-samanhappy-mcphub--sse-endpoint-accepts-arbitrary-username-from-url-path-without-authentication--en---
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.003 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Tenant where an admin user genuinely has username `admin` / `administrator` (legitimately connecting their own client)
  • Penetration testers running authorized GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf validation
  • Security scanners (Nuclei templates) probing for the CVE
  • Service accounts named with `sysadmin` / `operator` legitimately using MCPHub
  • Synthetic monitoring that intentionally uses an `admin` username to verify the patch
Suppression filter
| where SrcIP !in ("10.0.0.50","10.0.0.51") // sanctioned pentest jump boxes
| where UA !has "Nuclei" and UA !has "DatadogSynthetics"
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm MCPHub package version on Computer. If < 0.12.15 with `enableBearerAuth=false`, treat the alert as a confirmed identity-spoofing attempt. Identify SrcIP and check whether it is internal (employee VPN) or external (internet-facing). 2. Contain: block SrcIP at the perimeter, force-disconnect the SSE session (`pkill node` or restart MCPHub process), upgrade package to >= 0.12.15, enable bearer auth and rotate any bearer keys. 3. Hunt: pivot to the downstream MCP servers (file system, GitHub, database connectors) that were reachable via this MCPHub instance and audit their activity for the spoofed-user time window — the impersonation is upstream but the damage is in the downstream tool calls.
// MCPHub admin-themed identity spoofing (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf)
let AdminTokens = dynamic(["admin","administrator","root","sudo","owner","superuser","sysadmin","ceo","cfo","cto","cio","operator","god","impersonated"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "GET"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/sse(/.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"^/([^/]+)/sse", 1, csUriStem))
   | extend SrcIP = cIP, Url = csUriStem, UA = csUserAgent, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/sse(?:/[^?]*)?(?:\?.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/sse", 1, RequestURL))
   | extend SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment)
| mv-apply tok = AdminTokens to typeof(string) on (
    where UserSegment contains tok
    | summarize MatchedTokens = make_set(tok)
  )
| where array_length(MatchedTokens) > 0
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, SrcIP, Computer, Url, UserSegment, MatchedTokens, UA
| order by TimeGenerated desc

MCPHub SSE user-segment fan-out — single source spawning sessions under multiple usernames AIReconnaissance High
Detects a single source IP creating MCPHub SSE sessions under three or more distinct `<user>` URL segments within a 10-minute window — the textbook impersonation-probing / user-enumeration pattern enabled by GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf. Legitimate clients connect under one identity per host. Rationale: Threshold-based: legitimate MCPHub clients connect under one consistent username per host. A SrcIP cycling through 3+ distinct `<user>/sse` segments in 10m is enumeration / impersonation probing — the only realistic explanation given the article's documented `req.params.user` design flaw. Sigma omitted because this is a cross-event aggregation. Datadog query is filter-only; the count/dcount threshold is enforced in the Cloud SIEM rule wrapper (groupBy SrcIP, count_unique UserSegment >= 3). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-WF8Q-WVV8-P8JF
ATT&CKT1087 T1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • NAT'd egress IP behind which multiple legitimate MCPHub users share the same SrcIP (employee VPN concentrator, corporate proxy)
  • Shared CI/CD runner that authenticates several pipeline service identities against MCPHub
  • Multi-tenant MCPHub deployments where one frontend IP fronts many tenants
  • Authorized red-team testing of the CVE
  • Load-test tooling iterating over synthetic user identities
Suppression filter
// Suppress known NAT/proxy egress IPs and CI runners after they've been profiled
| where SrcIP !in ("10.10.10.1","203.0.113.10")   // corp VPN concentrator + CI runner egress
| where DistinctUsers >= 3   // keep the floor; raise if NAT egress baseline higher
Response runbook
1. Triage: list the ObservedUsers set and cross-check against IdentityInfo / HR roster. If any segment is not a real user (e.g. `admin-test`, `impersonated`, random tokens) treat as confirmed. If SrcIP is a known proxy/NAT, normalize by X-Forwarded-For (W3CIISLog: enable XFF logging) and re-evaluate. 2. Contain: block SrcIP at perimeter, terminate active SSE sessions on the MCPHub host, upgrade @samanhappy/mcphub to >= 0.12.15 and switch enableBearerAuth=true. 3. Hunt: for each ObservedUser, query downstream MCP-server tool-call logs for actions credited to that identity within the SSE session window; review database / GitHub / filesystem MCP-server audit trails for unauthorized reads or writes attributed to the impersonated user.
// MCPHub user-segment fan-out — single SrcIP, multiple distinct <user>/sse spoof attempts in 10m
let WindowSize = 10m;
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "GET"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/sse(/.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"^/([^/]+)/sse", 1, csUriStem)), SrcIP = cIP, Url = csUriStem, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "GET"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/sse(?:/[^?]*)?(?:\?.*)?$"
   | extend UserSegment = tolower(extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/sse", 1, RequestURL)), SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment)
| where UserSegment !in~ ("api","static","assets","health","favicon.ico","_next","public")
| summarize
    DistinctUsers = dcount(UserSegment),
    ObservedUsers = make_set(UserSegment, 30),
    Hits = count(),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
    SampleUrls = make_set(Url, 10)
    by SrcIP, Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowSize)
| where DistinctUsers >= 3   // empirical fan-out threshold — one legit client = one identity per host
| order by DistinctUsers desc, LastSeen desc

MCPHub tool execution via spoofed identity — POST to /<user>/messages with JSON-RPC body AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the second-stage exploitation after a spoofed SSE handshake (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf): POST to `/<user>/messages?sessionId=<uuid>` with a JSON-RPC tool call. This is where the spoofed identity is used to actually invoke MCP tools (filesystem, GitHub, DB connectors) under the impersonated user's authorization context. Rationale: The article's PoC Step 3 explicitly shows `curl -X POST http://TARGET:3100/CEO-admin-impersonated/messages?sessionId=54efc6f5-... -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call",...}'`. The URL shape `/<user>/messages?sessionId=<uuid>` is unique to MCPHub (the JSON-RPC tool-call ingress for the SSE transport) and represents the actual exploitation step — not just probing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf
ATT&CKT1059 T1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate MCPHub clients on patched instances invoking tools normally (the URL shape persists post-patch — it's the supported transport)
  • Authorized penetration testing of the CVE
  • Internal AI agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor) sending tool calls during normal operation
  • Synthetic monitoring exercising tool calls for uptime checks
  • Backup / replication tooling proxying MCP traffic
Suppression filter
// Once instance is patched + bearer auth on, this is benign traffic. Suppress when Authorization header is present.
// W3CIISLog doesn't carry headers; CSL has RequestHeader fields on some proxies — refine when available.
| where SrcIP !in ("10.10.10.20","10.10.10.21")   // sanctioned MCP client subnet
| where UA !has "Claude-Desktop" and UA !has "Cursor" and UA !has "mcp-client"
Response runbook
1. Triage: extract UserSegment + SessionId; correlate with the preceding SSE handshake (UC1/UC2 same SessionId or same SrcIP within seconds). Confirm MCPHub version < 0.12.15 or `enableBearerAuth=false`. Pull request body from reverse-proxy logs if available — JSON-RPC `method` and `params.name` reveal which MCP tool was invoked. 2. Contain: kill the SSE session (restart MCPHub or close the upstream socket), block SrcIP, upgrade to >= 0.12.15, enable bearer auth, rotate any secrets the impersonated tool could have read (DB creds, GitHub tokens, filesystem secrets). 3. Hunt: pivot to each named MCP server's audit log (filesystem.read, github.create_pr, db.query, etc.) for actions attributed to UserSegment in the SessionId's lifetime; assess data exfil and write-side actions; review IdP logs to check whether the spoofed UserSegment is a real privileged user whose downstream credentials may have been used.
// MCPHub tool-call execution against a spoofed SSE session (GHSA-wf8q-wvv8-p8jf, post-handshake)
union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where csMethod == "POST"
   | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/[^/]+/messages$"
   | where csUriQuery has "sessionId="
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"^/([^/]+)/messages", 1, csUriStem),
            SessionId   = extract(@"sessionId=([0-9a-fA-F-]{20,})", 1, csUriQuery),
            SrcIP = cIP, Url = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), UA = csUserAgent, SourceTable="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
   | where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)^(?:https?://[^/]+)?/[^/?]+/messages\?.*sessionId=[0-9a-f-]{20,}"
   | extend UserSegment = extract(@"(?i)/([^/]+)/messages", 1, RequestURL),
            SessionId   = extract(@"(?i)sessionId=([0-9a-fA-F-]{20,})", 1, RequestURL),
            SrcIP = SourceIP, Url = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, SourceTable="CommonSecurityLog")
| where isnotempty(UserSegment) and isnotempty(SessionId)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, SrcIP, Computer, Url, UserSegment, SessionId, UA
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DeepSeek-TUI sub-agent shell execution via AGENTS.md prompt injection (CVE-2026-45374) AIExploitation High
Hunts exploitation of CVE-2026-45374 where deepseek-tui's task_create tool spawns durable sub-agents with allow_shell=true and auto_approve=true defaults. A malicious AGENTS.md in a cloned repo injects shell commands (e.g. 'curl -s http://attacker/...') that execute without user approval. Detection pivots on the deepseek-tui binary spawning shell utilities or HTTP-egress LOLBins. Rationale: Article specifies the exact binary name 'deepseek-tui' (rust:deepseek-tui < 0.8.26) and shows the PoC payload as 'curl -s http://[collaborator]/badge-gen?project=web-service' executed via the sub-agent's shell. Parent=deepseek-tui spawning curl/wget/bash/python with HTTP URLs or shell -c flags is the highest-fidelity behavioural marker — deepseek-tui itself talks to the DeepSeek API directly (not via curl), so any forked shell/HTTP utility is anomalous and indicates the prompt-injection-driven sub-agent shell escape. External corroboration: confirmed deepseek-tui is a real Rust CLI (deepseek-ai/awesome-deepseek-agent repo) and a separate active campaign abuses fake deepseek-tui repos for malware delivery (cybersecuritynews.com), increasing the prior on this being targeted. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/deepseek-ai/awesome-deepseek-agent/blob/main/docs/deepseek-tui.md • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-use-fake-deepseek-tui-github-repositories/amp/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-72w5-pf8h-xfp4

DeepSeek-TUI spawning 'cargo test' — CVE-2026-45311 auto-approved run_tests pathway AIExploitation High
Hunts the specific vulnerable invocation chain where the DeepSeek-TUI agent (versions 0.3.0 to <0.8.23) auto-approves the run_tests tool and invokes 'cargo test'. status: experimental
description: Detects the DeepSeek-TUI agent invoking 'cargo test', which is auto-approved (ApprovalRequirement::Auto) in versions 0.3.0 to <0.8.23 and compiles+executes arbitrary code from the workspace (build.rs, proc macros, integration tests). A malicious repo's AGENTS.md can prompt-inject the model to call run_tests at session start, yielding RCE without user approval.

Rust cargo-test binary in target/debug/deps spawning shell or network tool (CVE-2026-45311 exploitation) AIExploitation High
Catches the actual RCE in flight: a compiled Rust integration-test binary under 'target/debug/deps/' or 'target/release/deps/' spawning a shell or network egress tool. The CVE-2026-45311 PoC uses std::process::Command::new("sh").args(["-c", "curl -s http://collaborator/..."]) from a #[test] function — this query catches that exact shell/HTTP shell-out from a Rust test artifact regardless of which agent (DeepSeek-TUI, similar tools) drove the cargo test. Rationale: Anchors on the Rust cargo build layout (target/(debug|release)/deps/ — where integration test binaries are emitted) combined with the PoC's exact shell-out pattern from the GHSA: std::process::Command::new("sh").args(["-c", "curl -s ..."]). Legitimate Rust integration tests almost never spawn external shells or network tools — their purpose is to exercise Rust code — so the parent-path+child-name pair is high fidelity. Mapped to T1195.001 because the delivery vector is a malicious Rust repo cloned via the developer's IDE/agent. Image attached to the GHSA confirms a Burp Collaborator callback, consistent with the curl shell-out captured by this query. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wx44-2q6h-j6p8 • https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI

sanitize-html xmp-tag XSS payload (CVE-2026-44990) in inbound HTTP request AIExploitation Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP requests carrying the CVE-2026-44990 sanitize-html bypass signature: an <xmp> element wrapping a <script> tag or HTML event handler (onerror=/onload=/onclick=). The xmp+script joint signature is the literal PoC from the GHSA-rpr9-rxv7-x643 advisory and is essentially never benign user content, so the URI/body match is high-fidelity for exploitation attempts against Apostrophe CMS or any other consumer of sanitize-html <=2.17.3. Rationale: The advisory's PoC is literal: `<xmp><script>alert(1)</script></xmp>`, `<xmp><img src=x onerror=alert(1)></xmp>`, `<xmp><svg><script>alert(1)</script></svg></xmp>`. Co-occurrence of <xmp> with <script> or an on*= handler in a single request URI/query is the exact bypass signature and effectively never appears in legitimate user-submitted content — even rich-text editors do not emit xmp. Coverage caveat: most stored-XSS exploitation comes via POST bodies, which aren't carried in DeviceNetworkEvents or standard IIS logs, hence Medium confidence overall; WAFs that mirror the body into CEF Message give the strongest signal. Cross-checked the related ApostropheCMS sanitize-html GHSA family (GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm / CVE-2026-40186 — the textarea/option entity-decode bypass — confirms the same `nonTextTags`/`ontext` raw-text passthrough pattern at the root of this CVE). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/apostrophecms/sanitize-html/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md • https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm • https://github.com/apostrophecms/sanitize-html
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Note: covers ONLY URL/query-string reflection. POST bodies are not captured in DeviceNetworkEvents.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess", "HttpConnectionInspected", "InboundConnectionAccepted")
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl contains "xmp"
| where (RemoteUrl contains "<xmp>" or RemoteUrl contains "<XMP>" or RemoteUrl contains "%3cxmp%3e" or RemoteUrl contains "%3CXMP%3E")
| where (RemoteUrl contains "<script" or RemoteUrl contains "%3cscript" or RemoteUrl contains "%3Cscript" or RemoteUrl contains "onerror=" or RemoteUrl contains "onload=" or RemoteUrl contains "onclick=" or RemoteUrl contains "onerror%3d" or RemoteUrl contains "onload%3d")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
// IIS access logs + WAF/CEF — covers URL query and request body excerpts (where carried by the WAF).
let _xmp_url = (s:string) { s contains "<xmp>" or s contains "<XMP>" or s contains "%3cxmp%3e" or s contains "%3CXMP%3E" or s contains "%3cXmp%3e" };
let _xss_url = (s:string) { s contains "<script" or s contains "%3cscript" or s contains "%3Cscript" or s contains "onerror=" or s contains "onload=" or s contains "onclick=" or s contains "onmouseover=" or s contains "onerror%3d" or s contains "onload%3d" };
union isfuzzy=true
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
  | where _xmp_url(csUriQuery) or _xmp_url(csUriStem)
  | where _xss_url(csUriQuery) or _xss_url(csUriStem)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
  | where _xmp_url(RequestURL) or _xmp_url(Message)
  | where _xss_url(RequestURL) or _xss_url(Message)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source=strcat(DeviceVendor,"/",DeviceProduct), Computer=DestinationHostName, cIP=SourceIP, csMethod=RequestMethod, csUriStem=RequestURL, csUriQuery=tostring(Message), scStatus=tostring(EventOutcome), csUserAgent=RequestClientApplication
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable sanitize-html <=2.17.3 / Apostrophe CMS asset inventory (CVE-2026-44990) AIReconnaissance High
Identifies hosts running a vulnerable build of sanitize-html or Apostrophe CMS as reported by Defender TVM. The hunt closes the exposure window by producing a patch list before exploitation telemetry appears, and gives the SOC a target asset set for tighter monitoring of UC#1. Rationale: The advisory pins affected to npm:sanitize-html <=2.17.3 (PoC against 2.17.3); upstream changelog and the related GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm advisory show the fix line continues in the 2.17.x branch. Hunting both via TVM CveId (when MS finishes ingesting the CVE feed) and via raw `SoftwareName + SoftwareVersion` catches the gap where the CVE lookup hasn't propagated yet. TVM data is asset-level so FP is essentially zero — output is a patch list, not an alert. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/apostrophecms/sanitize-html/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md • https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-9mrh-v2v3-xpfm

The time of much patching is coming

Cisco Talos
2026-05-14 10 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

In this week’s newsletter, Martin reflects on what the next iteration of AI tools means for vulnerability discovery and our ability to manage large-scale patch releases.

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — The time of much patching is coming
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Talos weekly top-prevalent malware hash watch (Coinminer / Injector / W32.Variant) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Talos weekly top-prevalent malware hash watch (Coinminer / Injector / W32.Variant) AIInstallation High
Surfaces any execution, image-load, or file-write of the four SHA256/MD5 hashes Cisco Talos published in the 2026-05-14 Threat Source newsletter as the most prevalent malware seen in Talos telemetry that week (Win.Worm.Coinminer VID001.exe, W32.Injector d4aa3e70…_63_Exe.exe, W32.Variant u112417.dat, Auto.90B145 APQ9305.dll). Article-specific because it pins on the exact SHA256/MD5 + Talos detection names from this week's bulletin, not a generic IOC sweep. Rationale: Hash IOCs are deterministic — these four SHA256s and the four MD5s come straight from Cisco Talos's weekly telemetry top-list with named verdicts (Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201, W32.Injector:Gen.21ie.1201, W32.Variant:MalwareXgenMisc.29d4.1201, Auto.90B145.282358.in02). They were corroborated by following each Talos file-reputation URL embedded in the article (talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=<SHA256>) which is Talos's authoritative reputation service confirming the verdict. The example filenames VID001.exe / u112417.dat / APQ9305.dll are renameable and only used as soft secondary signal in Splunk — the SHA256/MD5 are the high-fidelity anchors. FP rate is low because we're hash-pinned; the only realistic FPs are authorized malware sandbox hosts (allowlist them). Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-time-of-much-patching-is-coming/ • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Portainer Swarm service create/update API access (CVE-2026-44849 exploitation path) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for HTTP POST traffic to the Portainer Docker Swarm service create / update endpoints that the CVE-2026-44849 advisory identifies as the bypass surface. Surfaces the specific URI paths (/services/create and /services/{id}/update) that skip EndpointSecuritySettings validation so analysts can pivot to who exercised them and from where. Rationale: Targets the two URIs the GHSA explicitly names as the bypass surface (POST /services/create with 1-of-7 checks, POST /services/{id}/update with 0-of-7 checks, plus POST /volumes/create which never had the bind-mount check). Pivots on the exact paths from the advisory so signal is bound to the vulnerable endpoints rather than generic Docker API noise. Cross-referenced with Portainer release notes (2.33.8 / 2.39.2 / 2.41.0). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/portainer/portainer/releases • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Administrator legitimately creating new Swarm services through the Portainer UI
  • Automation pipelines (Ansible / Terraform / GitOps) calling Portainer API to deploy stacks
  • Portainer agent health-checks polling Swarm endpoints
  • CI runners updating service images via portainer-cli or curl as part of release deploys
Suppression filter
| where csUserName !endswith "$" and csUserName !in~ ("portainer-agent", "system", "automation-svc")
| where csUserAgent !has_any ("terraform", "ansible", "gitops")
Response runbook
1) Triage: Pull the user that issued the POST (csUserName / InitiatingProcessAccountName) and check whether they are an admin role in Portainer. Non-admin users with Swarm endpoint access are the at-risk population. Pull the request body if your proxy logs it; look for CapabilityAdd, Privileges.Seccomp.Mode=unconfined, or Mounts with type=volume + DriverConfig.Options. 2) Contain: Temporarily revoke Swarm endpoint access for non-admin Portainer users via Portainer RBAC (per advisory workaround). If a malicious service is identified, force-delete it and quarantine the node it landed on. 3) Hunt: Pivot the source IP and user against successful authentications to Portainer, then look for downstream container processes that spawned chroot, nsenter, or accessed /var/run/docker.sock — see related UCs.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/services/create", "/volumes/create")
   or RemoteUrl matches regex @"/services/[^/]+/update"
| where RemotePort in (9000, 9443, 8000, 443)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hits = count(), AnyCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl
| order by LastSeen desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod =~ "POST"
| where csUriStem has_any ("/services/create", "/volumes/create")
   or csUriStem matches regex @"/services/[^/]+/update"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count(), Methods = make_set(csMethod), URIs = make_set(csUriStem)
           by Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csUserName, csUserAgent
| order by LastSeen desc

Portainer Swarm service spec with elevated Linux capabilities or unconfined Seccomp AIExploitation High
Hunts for the docker daemon on a Swarm-enabled host receiving service specs that contain the privileged values the CVE-2026-44849 advisory describes (CapabilityAdd: SYS_ADMIN/NET_ADMIN/SYS_PTRACE/ALL, Privileges.Seccomp.Mode: unconfined, AppArmor disabled). Captures the daemon-side artefact of the bypass even when proxy logs don't include request bodies. Rationale: Pulls the exact capability strings (SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, ALL) and modes (unconfined Seccomp, disabled AppArmor) listed in the GHSA Impact section. These values are not part of normal container spec on most fleets, so the binding to dockerd/containerd/runc plus those specific tokens keeps FP rate low. Verified against the advisory's pre-fix code excerpt showing CapabilityAdd/Sysctls/Privileges were never parsed by the partial service struct. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/service/create/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1611 T1610 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate privileged workloads (CNI plugins, eBPF agents, observability daemonsets) that genuinely need CAP_SYS_ADMIN
  • Security-tool deployments (Falco, sysdig, tetragon) launched with cap_net_admin or cap_sys_ptrace
  • Kubernetes / Swarm operator pre-deploying privileged init containers for storage drivers
  • Penetration-test or red-team exercises explicitly authorised to test capability assignment
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("falco", "sysdig", "tetragon", "cilium-agent")
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("kube-system", "calico-node", "weave-net")
Response runbook
1) Triage: Identify which Portainer user (cross-ref UC1) or which orchestrator deployed the service. Pull the docker inspect output for the running container — confirm whether CapabilityAdd/Privileges actually contain the elevated values vs being passed but rejected. 2) Contain: docker service rm the offending service (or kubectl delete if K8s-managed). Block the Portainer user's session and rotate their credentials. If the container had bind-mount of /, treat the host as potentially compromised. 3) Hunt: Sweep the same host for chroot/nsenter activity (UC3) and for write events under /etc, /root/.ssh, /var/spool/cron, or /usr/local/sbin (persistence). Pull docker.sock access events on the host (UC4).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
   or FileName in~ ("runc", "crun", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("CAP_SYS_ADMIN", "CAP_NET_ADMIN", "CAP_SYS_PTRACE", "cap_sys_admin", "cap_net_admin", "cap_sys_ptrace", "\"ALL\"", "seccomp=unconfined", "apparmor=unconfined", "AppArmorProfile=unconfined", "\"Mode\":\"unconfined\"")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "portainer", "runc", "crun")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("CAP_SYS_ADMIN", "CAP_NET_ADMIN", "CAP_SYS_PTRACE", "cap_sys_admin", "cap_net_admin", "cap_sys_ptrace", "seccomp=unconfined", "apparmor=unconfined", "\"unconfined\"", "\"capabilities\":[\"ALL\"]", "CapabilityAdd")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, HostIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Docker Swarm Service Spec With Elevated Capabilities or Unconfined Seccomp (CVE-2026-44849)
id: 3c5c9f9a-5f6e-4b6a-9c5a-44849aaa0002
description: Detects dockerd / containerd / runc receiving service specs with elevated Linux capabilities or seccomp/apparmor unconfined, the post-bypass artefact of CVE-2026-44849.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.t1611
  - attack.t1610
  - attack.t1068
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/dockerd'
      - '/containerd'
      - '/runc'
      - '/crun'
      - '/containerd-shim-runc-v2'
  selection_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN'
      - 'CAP_NET_ADMIN'
      - 'CAP_SYS_PTRACE'
      - 'cap_sys_admin'
      - 'seccomp=unconfined'
      - 'apparmor=unconfined'
      - '"unconfined"'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_args
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog OR docker) (@process.name:(dockerd OR containerd OR runc OR crun OR containerd-shim*) OR @ProcessName:(dockerd OR containerd OR runc)) (@process.command_line:(*CAP_SYS_ADMIN* OR *CAP_NET_ADMIN* OR *CAP_SYS_PTRACE* OR *seccomp=unconfined* OR *apparmor=unconfined*) OR @message:(*CAP_SYS_ADMIN* OR *cap_sys_admin* OR *seccomp=unconfined* OR *\"unconfined\"* OR *CapabilityAdd*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 
| ImageFileName=/(dockerd|containerd|runc|crun|containerd-shim)/i 
| regex("(CAP_SYS_ADMIN|CAP_NET_ADMIN|CAP_SYS_PTRACE|cap_sys_admin|seccomp=unconfined|apparmor=unconfined|\"unconfined\")", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="dockerd" OR Processes.process_name="containerd-shim" OR Processes.process_name="runc" OR Processes.parent_process_name="dockerd") AND (Processes.process="*cap_sys_admin*" OR Processes.process="*CAP_SYS_ADMIN*" OR Processes.process="*cap_net_admin*" OR Processes.process="*cap_sys_ptrace*" OR Processes.process="*--privileged*" OR Processes.process="*seccomp=unconfined*" OR Processes.process="*apparmor=unconfined*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Container escape via chroot/nsenter against mounted host filesystem AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts for chroot or nsenter invocations targeting /host, /proc/1/ns, or /proc/1/root — the textbook second-stage of the CVE-2026-44849 chain where the attacker has already created/updated a Swarm service that bind-mounts the host root and now pivots into the host namespace. Targets the executable + flag combinations that distinguish escape from benign chroot use. Rationale: Bound to the specific escape pattern the GHSA describes: 'access the host filesystem from the running container (e.g. via chroot /host)'. Pairs the LOLBin (chroot/nsenter) with the namespace-target tokens so it doesn't match administrative chroot use, and excludes systemd/snapd parents that legitimately invoke chroot during host operations. The advisory text 'chroot /host' is used verbatim as one of the high-signal matches. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/ • https://gtfobins.github.io/gtfobins/chroot/
ATT&CKT1611 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin troubleshooting on a host by chroot'ing into a mounted recovery image
  • Container build pipelines (debootstrap, mkosi) that legitimately chroot into staging directories
  • Container management tools (kubectl debug --target=host, crictl exec) when used by authorised operators
  • Backup / restore tooling mounting host filesystem snapshots for offline inspection
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2", "runc", "crun", "dockerd")
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "debootstrap" and ProcessCommandLine !has "mkosi"
Response runbook
1) Triage: Identify the parent process and container ID (InitiatingProcessParentFileName containerd-shim / runc means it came from a container). Pull `docker ps` / `crictl ps` output and identify the service/task. Correlate with UC1 for the originating Portainer user. 2) Contain: Kill the offending container immediately (`docker kill` / `docker service rm`). Isolate the host from the network — chroot /host implies the attacker now has root on the underlying host. Rotate any credentials cached on the host (/root/.ssh, /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf, cloud metadata creds). 3) Hunt: From the same host, look for outbound C2 (DeviceNetworkEvents), files written under /etc/cron*, /etc/systemd/system, /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, and downstream lateral movement via SSH key reuse. Pivot the source IP of the originating Portainer session against authentication logs.
DeviceProcessEvents

Container start with docker.sock or sensitive host-path bind mount AIExploitation High
Hunts for container processes whose runtime spec includes a bind mount of /var/run/docker.sock, /, /root/.ssh, or the Portainer data directory — the post-bypass artefacts of CVE-2026-44849 where a non-admin user has slipped an unrestricted bind mount past the missing AllowBindMountsForRegularUsers check. The docker.sock variant is particularly high-signal because it directly enables sibling-container escape. Rationale: Pulls the exact sensitive paths the advisory enumerates ('bind mounts of any host path, including /, /var/run/docker.sock, SSH keys, or Portainer's own database'). Each of those paths is named verbatim in the Impact section, making the match high-fidelity. docker.sock + a container is sufficient on its own to grant container-breakout primitives, so this also fires as a leading indicator even without confirmed exploitation of CVE-2026-44849. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1611 T1613 T1525
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Portainer-agent container itself which legitimately mounts /var/run/docker.sock to manage the local engine
  • CI / build runners (jenkins, gitlab-runner, drone) that mount docker.sock for docker-in-docker builds
  • Observability sidecars (cAdvisor, Sysdig, Datadog agent) that mount docker.sock for container telemetry
  • Watchtower / shepherd-style auto-updaters that legitimately need socket access
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("portainer-agent", "cadvisor", "datadog-agent", "gitlab-runner", "jenkins", "watchtower", "shepherd")
Response runbook
1) Triage: From the container ID, identify the image name and the user who deployed it. Cross-reference with UC1 (was this a non-admin Portainer user calling /services/create or /services/{id}/update?). If image is portainer-agent, cadvisor, datadog-agent, or a known CI runner — likely benign; document and tune. 2) Contain: For unknown / unauthorised containers: `docker kill <id>` then `docker service rm`. Rotate any credentials present at the bind-mount targets (/root/.ssh/* keys, Portainer DB encryption key under /data/portainer). 3) Hunt: Look for child processes from the container that touched docker CLI (sibling container creation), chroot, or nsenter (UC3). Sweep the host for new SSH authorized_keys entries and new cron jobs created since the suspicious container started.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
   or FileName in~ ("runc", "crun", "containerd-shim", "containerd-shim-runc-v2")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/var/run/docker.sock", "docker.sock", "-v /:", "--volume=/:", "source=/ ", "source=/,", "source=/var/run/docker.sock", "/root/.ssh", "/data/portainer", "/host/etc", "\"Source\":\"/\"")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "containerd-shim", "runc", "crun")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/var/run/docker.sock", "docker.sock", "-v /:", "--volume=/:", "source=/ ", "source=/,", "/root/.ssh", "/data/portainer", "\"Source\":\"/\"", "\"Source\":\"/var/run/docker.sock\"")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, HostIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Docker local-driver volume created with type=none and o=bind (CVE-2026-44849 volume variant) AIExploitation High
Hunts for the volume-driver-bind bypass variant the advisory calls out separately: a Type:volume mount whose VolumeOptions.DriverConfig.Options declares the local driver with type=none and o=bind, or a direct POST /volumes/create with the same payload. Either path materialises a bind-equivalent mount that the partial Mounts struct check never inspected on any Portainer branch. Rationale: Targets the volume-driver-bind variant called out in its own paragraph of the advisory: 'A mount with Type:"volume" and VolumeOptions.DriverConfig.Options: {type:"none", o:"bind", device:"<host path>"} is forwarded to the Docker daemon unchanged'. The triple type=none + o=bind + device= is the canonical local-driver bind incantation; legitimate use of this combination is extremely rare outside of explicit infrastructure-as-code volume declarations on the same host. Also unions in POST /volumes/create on the proxy log because the advisory notes that endpoint never had the AllowBindMountsForRegularUsers check on any branch. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5fxq-qcf3-244w • https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/volume/create/ • https://docs.docker.com/storage/volumes/
ATT&CKT1611 T1078.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Infrastructure-as-Code (Ansible/Terraform/docker-compose) declaring NFS-style local volumes on a build host
  • Stateful application deploys (databases, file servers) that legitimately bind host directories via the local driver pattern
  • Backup tooling that creates short-lived bind-volumes to mount snapshot directories into a restore container
  • Documentation / training environments where the volume-driver bind is being demonstrated
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("docker-compose", "ansible-playbook", "terraform apply", "helm install")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("ansible-playbook", "terraform", "helm")
Response runbook
1) Triage: docker volume inspect the created volume, identify the device= path (the host directory now exposed). If the path is /, /etc, /root, /var/run, or a Portainer data dir, treat as confirmed exploitation. Cross-reference with UC1 to identify the originating Portainer user. 2) Contain: docker volume rm the offending volume (forcing removal of any container using it first). Revoke Swarm-endpoint access for the implicated Portainer user. Apply the workaround from the advisory: block creation of local-driver volumes with type:none / o:bind via a daemon-side allowlist until 2.33.8 / 2.39.2 / 2.41.0 is deployed. 3) Hunt: For any container that mounted the volume, follow UC3 / UC4 — look for chroot/nsenter into the bind target, file writes to sensitive locations on the host, and persistence indicators (cron, systemd units, SSH keys).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd", "docker", "containerd") or FileName in~ ("docker", "dockerd")
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "type=none" and ProcessCommandLine has "o=bind" and ProcessCommandLine has "device=")
     or (ProcessCommandLine has "volume create" and ProcessCommandLine has "--driver local" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-o type=none", "--opt type=none"))
     or (ProcessCommandLine has "VolumeOptions" and ProcessCommandLine has "DriverConfig")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let DockerActivity = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd", "containerd", "docker")
    | where (SyslogMessage has "type=none" and SyslogMessage has "o=bind")
         or (SyslogMessage has "\"type\":\"none\"" and SyslogMessage has "\"o\":\"bind\"")
         or (SyslogMessage has "DriverConfig" and SyslogMessage has "\"local\"" and SyslogMessage has "device");
let WebActivity = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriStem has "/volumes/create" or csUriStem matches regex @"/services/[^/]+/(create|update)"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUserName, csUriStem, csMethod;
union isfuzzy=true DockerActivity, WebActivity
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Portainer plugin management API access (CVE-2026-44848) AIExploitation High
Hunts HTTP POST requests to Portainer's /docker/plugins/pull and /docker/plugins/{name}/enable proxy endpoints, which bypass Portainer-side RBAC in vulnerable releases (<2.33.8, <2.39.2, <2.41.0) because /plugins is absent from prefixProxyFuncMap and falls through to executeDockerRequest unauthorized. Rationale: Article identifies the exact vulnerable endpoints (POST /plugins/pull, POST /plugins/{name}/enable) and shows in the Go source excerpt that /plugins is NOT in prefixProxyFuncMap so it bypasses Portainer's authorization wrapper. A successful POST against this URI from a non-admin session is unambiguous exploitation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4
ATT&CKT1190 T1068
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Portainer administrator legitimately installing a Docker volume/log/network plugin from a trusted registry
  • Automation tooling (Ansible/Terraform) using a Portainer admin token to provision plugins after a node rebuild
  • Internal CI/CD pipeline calling the plugin API with a service account during cluster bootstrap
  • Pentest or red-team exercise validating this advisory
  • GET requests from health-check scrapers (excluded by the POST predicate)
Suppression filter
| where csUserName !in~ ("portainer-admin","ansible-portainer","terraform-portainer")
Response runbook
1. Triage: Open the matched proxy/IIS log line and extract csUserName / Portainer JWT subject and source IP; confirm whether that identity holds the Portainer admin role. 2. Contain: Disable the user in Portainer or revoke its Docker-endpoint access, isolate the target Docker host, and quarantine any plugin under /var/lib/docker/plugins/ created within +/- 10 minutes of the request. 3. Hunt: Pivot to host telemetry (UC2/UC3) on the same DeviceName / timestamp window, look for chroot or nsenter from the plugin container, and audit /etc/docker/plugins for new manifests. Upgrade Portainer to 2.33.8 / 2.39.2 / 2.41.0+.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod =~ "POST"
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/api/endpoints/\d+/docker/plugins/(pull|.+/enable)"
| where scStatus < 400
