Docker plugin runtime spawned from /var/lib/docker/plugins/ on host (CVE-2026-44848) AIInstallation High
Hunts Linux process executions whose binary path begins with /var/lib/docker/plugins/<digest>/rootfs/ and whose parent is dockerd/containerd/runc. Any post-exploit plugin pushed through the unauthorized /plugins/pull + /plugins/{name}/enable chain lands here and executes as root with whatever capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, host bind mounts) the plugin manifest requested. Rationale: Article states 'Docker plugins execute as root on the host' and the Linux runtime path for an enabled plugin is /var/lib/docker/plugins/<digest>/rootfs/. Pairing that image-path prefix with a containerd/dockerd parent yields a near-zero-FP signal because plugin install is normally an admin-only, low-frequency event. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4 • https://docs.docker.com/engine/extend/plugin_api/
ATT&CKT1068 T1611 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Administrator legitimately installing a known Docker volume plugin (rexray, vieux/sshfs)
  • CI/CD pipeline reinstalling a vetted log driver plugin after a node rebuild
  • Kubernetes CSI plugin operator installing a storage driver
  • Backup software (Velero/Restic) shipping a Docker volume plugin
  • Docker engine upgrade re-creating plugin rootfs paths
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("rexray","vieux/sshfs","docker/telemetry","weaveworks/net-plugin")
Response runbook
1. Triage: Read /var/lib/docker/plugins/<digest>/config.json and inspect for CAP_SYS_ADMIN, propagatedMount, host-path bind mounts, or an untrusted registry origin; correlate with UC1 W3CIISLog/proxy events on the same host+time to identify the Portainer user. 2. Contain: `docker plugin disable <name>` then `docker plugin rm -f <name>`, isolate the host from the network, snapshot for forensics, and rotate any credentials reachable from the host. 3. Hunt: Search the cluster for the same plugin digest, audit other Portainer endpoints accessed by that user, and review auth.log + bash history for chroot/nsenter/mount activity originating from the plugin container.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath startswith "/var/lib/docker/plugins/"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dockerd","containerd","containerd-shim","containerd-shim-runc-v2","runc")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName startswith "/var/lib/docker/plugins/"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("dockerd","containerd","containerd-shim","containerd-shim-runc-v2","runc")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Docker plugin runtime executed from /var/lib/docker/plugins (CVE-2026-44848)
id: a2d96f74-6ac0-4b0c-9c2c-1c0a8b7a4f31
description: Detects any Linux process whose image path lives under /var/lib/docker/plugins/ and is spawned by the Docker daemon, containerd, or runc. Triggered by the CVE-2026-44848 post-exploit chain when a non-admin Portainer user pulls and enables an attacker-controlled plugin.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:

  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1611
  - attack.t1610
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|startswith: '/var/lib/docker/plugins/'
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/dockerd'
      - '/containerd'
      - '/containerd-shim'
      - '/containerd-shim-runc-v2'
      - '/runc'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:(linux.auditd OR linux.sysmon) @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.executable.path:/var/lib/docker/plugins/* OR @process.command_line:*/var/lib/docker/plugins/*) (@process.parent.name:dockerd OR @process.parent.name:containerd OR @process.parent.name:containerd-shim OR @process.parent.name:containerd-shim-runc-v2 OR @process.parent.name:runc)

Docker daemon plugin install/enable event from non-admin context (CVE-2026-44848) AIInstallation Medium
Surfaces dockerd syslog entries recording plugin pull/install/enable operations. Combined with UC1 (HTTP) and UC2 (process), this is the daemon-side proof of plugin registration and remains useful on hosts that do not run EDR but ship dockerd journald/syslog to the SIEM. Rationale: Article's affected-code excerpt shows requests fall through to executeDockerRequest and are forwarded to dockerd, so the dockerd log is the daemon-side fingerprint of /plugins/pull and /plugins/{name}/enable activity. This UC corroborates UC1+UC2 on hosts without EDR. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rrmm-9v76-h3p4
ATT&CKT1610 T1068
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admin operator running `docker plugin install` from the CLI for a vetted plugin
  • Docker engine restart replaying plugin-enable events from /var/lib/docker/plugins
  • Swarm rebuild rolling plugins back onto fresh nodes
  • Kubernetes node lifecycle reinstalling logging/storage drivers
  • Plugin upgrade as part of routine patching
Suppression filter
| where PluginName !in~ ("rexray","vieux/sshfs","weaveworks/net-plugin","docker/telemetry")
Response runbook
1. Triage: Extract the plugin name + digest from the dockerd line, list current plugins (`docker plugin ls --no-trunc`), and inspect the manifest for excessive privileges or an unknown registry. 2. Contain: Disable and remove the plugin (`docker plugin disable <name>` then `docker plugin rm -f <name>`), then rotate any credentials accessible from the host. 3. Hunt: Pivot to UC1 (proxy/IIS) by host+timestamp to find which Portainer user triggered the install, and to UC2 to enumerate binaries that ran from /var/lib/docker/plugins.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName in~ ("dockerd","containerd")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/plugins/pull","/plugins/","plugin enabled","plugin pull","plugin install","POST /plugins")
| extend PluginOp = extract(@"plugins?[/=](pull|enable|install)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend PluginName = extract(@"plugin[ =:]([A-Za-z0-9_/.:@-]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| where isnotempty(PluginOp)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, PluginOp, PluginName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR docker) @process.name:dockerd (@message:*plugins/pull* OR @message:*"plugin enabled"* OR @message:*"plugin pull"* OR @message:*"plugin install"* OR @message:*"POST /plugins/"*)
ENDPOINT
index=* sourcetype IN ("linux:syslog","linux:journald") process_name=dockerd ("plugins/pull" OR "plugin enabled" OR "plugin pull" OR "plugin install" OR "POST /plugins/")
| rex field=_raw "plugin(?:s)?[/=](?<plugin_op>pull|enable|install)"
| rex field=_raw "plugin[ =:](?<plugin_name>[A-Za-z0-9_/.:@\-]+)"
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(plugin_name) as plugin_name by host plugin_op
| sort 0 -lastTime

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44848")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-44848")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
